updates.label: KUTV publishes body-camera footage of Officer Kyle Pitt rescuing woman from overpass

descriptionParagraphs.text: On October 29, 2026, KUTV 2News published a report about American Fork Police Officer
Kyle Bradley Pitt

helping a woman experiencing a mental health crisis on a highway overpass. Based on the body-camera footage, the incident occurred on August 22, 2026. As she slipped through a gap in the fence, Pitt grabbed her and pulled her back to safety.

Among the examples of poor handling of mental health crises that have drawn public concern, this incident stands out as an example of good crisis response and officer compassion. It reflects the kind of compassionate policing and thoughtful handling of mental health crises that the AFPD Accountability Project strives to recognize and promote.

updates.label: K-9 records obtained through GRAMA request

descriptionParagraphs.text: On October 27, 2026, AFPD Accountability obtained American Fork Police Department K-9 records through a Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA) records request.

The records include a list of 306 K-9 support incidents covering January 1, 2025–October 13, 2026, with incident numbers, reported dates and times, area codes, agencies, and dispositions. A separate July 2025–July 2026 spreadsheet lists cases and zones, interest and search indicators, recorded finds, and apprehension-related entries.
The records also include a likely connection to
Reckless Ben

: K-9 support case 26AF02009 was reported March 9, 2026, at 7:59:44 p.m. and is listed with “No Find” in the spreadsheet. The connection is not confirmed, but highly likely: the timestamp falls during that incident, and the case number is only two numbers after the associated harassment report, 26AF02007. This suggests the K-9 officer may have submitted a separate incident report for the same encounter.

updates.label: KSL’s Andrew Adams interviews Chief Cameron Paul

descriptionParagraphs.text: KSL confirmed that reporter Andrew Adams interviewed American Fork Police Chief
Cameron Paul
. KSL described the interview as being about domestic violence and said it would be released at a future date.
It is not known whether the
Reckless Ben case
or other controversies involving the AFPD were discussed.
Clearly Established

attorney Brandon Grable reviews Daniel Sroka’s released transcript of his September 16, 2026 meeting with Chief Cameron Paul. The video includes interview excerpts with Sroka, plaintiffs Steven Allen and Sheldon Norcross, and their attorney, Solomon Radner.

Grable examines the warrant affidavit, handcuffing and transporting the occupants, Sheldon Norcross’s phone seizure, missing and muted body-camera recordings, redactions, and the chief’s promised follow-up. He also addresses the portions of the police response that the chief continued to defend.
The video distinguishes the citizen-prepared meeting transcript from an audio recording and attributes the chief’s remarks to that transcript.

updates.label: Daniel Sroka’s September 16, 2026 interview with Chief Paul — revised transcript

descriptionParagraphs.text: Daniel Sroka finished refining the transcript of his September 16, 2026 interview with American Fork Police Chief Cameron Paul.
The rough transcript was generated using an automated transcription app, then corrected and revised with AI assistance. Eric Seamons and Daniel Sroka subsequently made manual revisions.
Read the September 16, 2026 interview transcript — PDF
The original app transcript and successive corrected drafts are preserved alongside the final participant-reviewed version, so readers can follow the corrections and review process.

$override.label: Daniel Sroka discusses meetings with Chief Paul on Clearly Established

descriptionParagraphs.text: American Fork resident Daniel Sroka appeared on
Clearly Established
to discuss his two meetings with Chief Cameron Paul about the March police encounters involving
Reckless Ben
and others.
Sroka described the chief’s changed assessment of the arrests and search warrant, his acknowledgment of mistakes, and the need for public accountability.
The video also features interviews with plaintiffs Sheldon Norcross and Steven Allen and their attorney, Solomon Radner.
